title: engine-loop episode — one run of one arm
description: An episode is the atomic observation: a single arm executed once, with its build fingerprint, its measurements and the artifact that produced them. It carries NO interpretation — interpretation lives in `decision` and `lesson`. The two hard gates are (1) a missing build fingerprint makes the episode incomparable and therefore useless, and (2) an unstable answer_md5 means the run was not deterministic and must not be used as evidence.

episode_id.description: eng-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHMMSS>-<arm>-r<rep>. The timestamp is taken from the server log filename, never typed by hand.

goal.description: One sentence: what this run was trying to establish. Required, because an observation with no question attached cannot be turned into a decision.

declared_purpose.description: What this arm claims to prove, copied verbatim from the ARMS table in scripts/check/decode_sweep.py so the claim cannot drift from the arm.

usable_for_throughput.description: false for probe arms (GGML_SCHED_DEBUG, CGC_S1_DBG, ...) and for upper-bound probes whose output is deliberately wrong. A false here makes decode_tps unquotable, not merely unreliable.

build.description: Three md5 prefixes, or null when the artifact does not record them. NULL IS NOT A WARNING, IT IS A VERDICT: an episode with build == null MUST have usable_as_evidence == false, because a throughput or bit-identical number whose binaries are unknown cannot be compared to anything -- not to another arm, and not to itself a day later after a rebuild. validate.py enforces the implication. Historical rows predating fingerprint recording (scripts/check/decode_sweep.py only started writing it on 2026-09-15) are emitted with build == null rather than dropped: they are still usable as tool-trace examples, just never as measurements.

kind.description: Which artifact shape this observation has. The emitter sets it; it is what tells a reader which of the optional blocks below are meaningful instead of merely absent. `sweep`/`interleave`/`bench` carry a generation (so answer_md5 is mandatory); `gate`/`oracle` verify logits and carry no throughput.

answer_md5.description: The SET of answer digests observed across rounds. Size > 1 is the non-determinism alarm. Mandatory (non-empty) whenever decode_tps.median is a number, i.e. whenever a generation actually happened.

oracle.description: gate/oracle episodes: the logits digest set and whether it matched the reference.

phase_ms.description: Steady-state medians parsed from the CGC-GPUTIME / CGC-DECPROF lines of the artifact log. gpu_busy_sum may exceed 100% of the step because kernels overlap; `gap` is the GPU-clock window with nothing running.

diagnostic_keys.description: Env keys the gate had to whitelist because they ARE the proposition under test. Recorded so a pass cannot be read as broader than it is.

log.description: $REPO-relative, sanitized. null when the artifact is not a server log (a bench matrix, a gate dump, an oracle .jsonl) — those point at their own file via `source` instead of pretending to have a log.

source.description: The file this episode was emitted from (repo-relative). Provenance for re-emission and for auditing the emitter itself.

usable_as_evidence.description: false when the answer was unstable, the fingerprint is missing, or the arm is a deliberate-wrong-output probe. It gates QUOTING A NUMBER, not being cited at all: an unstable episode is precisely the evidence a decision needs in order to establish non-determinism (see dec-20260915-2115-s1-divergence-is-per-layer-not-global, which rests on a row with usable_as_evidence == false). Such a row must therefore still carry the observed digest set in obs.answer_md5 and name the instability in caveats, so the structural claim can be checked without re-running anything.

caveats.description: Machine-checkable honesty. A reader must be able to reconstruct why a number is or is not quotable without reading the log.
